label: AGENT REVIEW — AUTHORISED BY OWNER
method: Automated accessibility-tree and keyboard checks with Playwright/Chromium on :3200 (synthetic 40-chapter story) + axe WCAG 2.1 AA on all seven workspaces. NO screen reader was used.

HR-16.Q1.note: Automated: first Tab = 'Skip to content', Enter moves focus to main. Before the fix this failed when the saved layout reopened the AI panel (fixed).

HR-16.Q2.note: Automated: nav 'Workspaces' with 8 named items; aria-current=page only on Write.

HR-16.Q3.note: Automated: editor is role=textbox 'Chapter text', aria-multiline=true (was unnamed — fixed); formatting toolbar role=toolbar; Draft/Edit is a radiogroup.

HR-16.Q4.note: Automated: heading 'AI Assistant' receives focus on open; Rewrite/Generate/Versions are tabs; Close returns focus to the 'AI assistant' button.

HR-16.Q5.note: Automated: Plan and World each expose one tablist with exactly one aria-selected tab.

HR-16.Q6.note: Automated: Continuity opens with focus on its H1; 'Back to all analyses' returns focus to the Continuity card.

HR-16.Q7.note: Automated: Ctrl+K opens one dialog named 'Command palette' with a combobox search field, focused.

HR-16.Q8.value: None — INCOMPLETE — REAL SCREEN-READER REVIEW REQUIRED. Automated checks only: Playwright 1.x / Chromium headless accessibility tree + @axe-core/playwright.

HR-16.Q9.value: Fixed during the review: (1) AI panel took focus on load when restored from the saved layout, bypassing the skip link; (2) manuscript editor had no role or name; (3) Story Bible scroll area not keyboard-focusable (axe serious). Remaining observation: the palette search field's name comes only from its placeholder (no aria-label). Not checked at all: speech output, verbosity, live-region announcements, reading order as spoken.

result_reasoning: INCOMPLETE — REAL SCREEN-READER REVIEW REQUIRED. Every step passes the automated accessibility-tree check after three fixes, and axe reports no violations on the seven workspaces with real data; but the MV-8.4 expected result is about what a screen reader announces, which only an NVDA/VoiceOver session can confirm.
